paragraphs: Children in care in Redcar and Cleveland are looked after by Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council's fostering service, shown above with the independent agencies that cover the borough. The council recruits through Foster with North East, the regional partnership, and its local fostering team and training venues are in the borough, so children can stay close to the schools and people they know. The council has said the number of children it cares for has risen sharply over the past decade, leaving it short of foster carers, and it wants families, couples and single people from every background.

Carers can offer emergency care at any hour, short-term care lasting days or months, long-term care for children who cannot go home, short breaks for disabled children, support care that helps birth families stay together, respite for other carers, parent and child placements, and family and friends care. You do not have to choose just one.

To apply you need to be over 21, with no upper age limit, and to own or rent a home with a spare bedroom. You can be single, married or living together, though couples need to have been together for two years. You can be working, not working or retired. Convictions must be declared but do not rule you out unless they involve offences against children, and the council will not approve smokers to care for children under five unless they commit to stopping.

After an enquiry and a home visit you join about three days of Skills to Foster training, then the checks, a medical paid for by the council, and a home study assessment. The council expects the whole process to take six to eight months before you go to its fostering panel. Approved carers get a supervising social worker, an out-of-hours helpline, local support groups and ongoing training, along with an allowance, a fee and mileage, and the council's support page describes a council tax exemption worth up to £1,500 a year.
Nearby, see our pages for Middlesbrough, Stockton-on-Tees and Hartlepool.
